\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{مرور} \fa{کردن} (morur kardan)}{مرور کردن (morur kardan)}]{\fa{مرور} \fa{کردن} (morur kardan) — to revise, to go over}

\label{lesson:FA-C401-morur-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a scholarship, then the Persian for a course credit.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{مرور} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{مرور} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{morur kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to revise, to go over\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{قبل} \fa{از} \fa{امتحان} \fa{همه} \fa{درسها} \fa{را} \fa{مرور} \fa{کردم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{qabl az emtehân hame-ye darshâ râ morur kardam.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Before the exam I went over all the lessons.
\end{quote}

\emph{Morur} \textquotedblleft{}passing over\textquotedblright{} + \emph{kardan} (stem \emph{kon-}).

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{مرور}} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{murūr} \textquotedblleft{}passing\textquotedblright{}: to revise is to pass over the lessons again. \emph{Kardan} \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{} is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{morur kardan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{morur kardan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{morur kardan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a scholarship, then the Persian for a course credit, then say \emph{morur kardan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{مرور} \fa{کردن} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To revise, to go over\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{تمرکز} \fa{کردن} (tamarkoz kardan)}{تمرکز کردن (tamarkoz kardan)}]{\fa{تمرکز} \fa{کردن} (tamarkoz kardan) — to concentrate}

\label{lesson:FA-C401-tamarkoz-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a course credit, then the Persian for to revise.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{تمرکز} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{تمرکز} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{tamarkoz kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to concentrate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{وقتی} \fa{تلویزیون} \fa{روشن} \fa{است} \fa{نمیتوانم} \fa{تمرکز} \fa{کنم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{vaqti televiziyon roshan ast nemitavânam tamarkoz konam.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
When the television is on I cannot concentrate.
\end{quote}

\emph{Tamarkoz} \textquotedblleft{}concentration\textquotedblright{} + \emph{kardan}. It takes \emph{ruye}: \emph{ruye chizi tamarkoz kardan}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{تمرکز}} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{tamarkuz}, a verbal noun built on \emph{markaz} \textquotedblleft{}centre\textquotedblright{}: to concentrate is to gather at the centre.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{تقلب} \fa{کردن} (taqallob kardan)}{تقلب کردن (taqallob kardan)}]{\fa{تقلب} \fa{کردن} (taqallob kardan) — to cheat}

\label{lesson:FA-C401-taqallob-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to revise, then the Persian for to concentrate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{تقلب} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{تقلب} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{taqallob kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to cheat\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{در} \fa{امتحان} \fa{تقلب} \fa{کرد} \fa{و} \fa{مردود} \fa{شد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{u dar emtehân taqallob kard va mardud shod.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He cheated in the exam and failed.
\end{quote}

\emph{Taqallob} \textquotedblleft{}cheating, fraud\textquotedblright{} + \emph{kardan}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{تقلب}} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{taqallub}, a verbal noun usually explained as turning over or changing; in Persian it is cheating.
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{جزوه} (jozve)}{جزوه (jozve)}]{\fa{جزوه} (jozve) — lecture notes, a handout}

\label{lesson:FA-C401-jozve}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to concentrate, then the Persian for to cheat.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{جزوه}}
\textbf{\fa{جزوه}} (\emph{jozve}) — \textquotedblleft{}lecture notes, a handout\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{جزوه} \fa{استاد} \fa{را} \fa{از} \fa{دوستم} \fa{گرفتم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{jozve-ye ostâd râ az dustam gereftam.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I got the professor's lecture notes from my friend.
\end{quote}

Plural \emph{jozvehâ}. Students lend and copy each other's \emph{jozve} before exams.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{جزوه}} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{juz'} \textquotedblleft{}a part, a section\textquotedblright{}: a booklet that is one part of a course.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{تکلیف} (taklif)}{تکلیف (taklif)}]{\fa{تکلیف} (taklif) — homework, an assignment; a duty}

\label{lesson:FA-C401-taklif}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to cheat, then the Persian for lecture notes.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{تکلیف}}
\textbf{\fa{تکلیف}} (\emph{taklif}) — \textquotedblleft{}homework, an assignment; a duty\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{بچه} \fa{ها} \fa{بعد} \fa{از} \fa{شام} \fa{تکلیفشان} \fa{را} \fa{انجام} \fa{دادند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bachche hâ ba'd az shâm taklifeshân râ anjâm dâdand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The children did their homework after dinner.
\end{quote}

Plural \emph{takâlif}, an Arabic broken plural. \emph{Taklif-e shab} — homework.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{تکلیف}} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{taklīf} \textquotedblleft{}imposing a task, a charge\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
